note: Viking raids on West Francia, including Paris (845, 885), led to Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte and Normandy.

_quarry.structural_significance: Viking Seine and Loire raids (840s–880s) systematically destroyed the Carolingian administrative infrastructure in western Francia—burning monasteries, eliminating record-keeping, disrupting fiscal networks—accelerating the fragmentation of royal authority and the militarisation of local power into counts and bishops who managed their own defences; this structural consequence, not the raids themselves, was the mechanism transforming West Francia into feudal France.
